subject: SIG: questions about ephemeral session keys, TLS termination, and rotation evidence
body:
From: Rachel Adams <soc@securebank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: SecureBank Compliance <compliance@securebank.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: ephemeral session keys / TLS termination / rotation evidence

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking our SIG queue item. We need more detail on three areas to complete the cryptography section:

1) TLS termination: where does TLS terminate for customer traffic (edge LB, ingress, model host)? Do you perform TLS termination at the load balancer and re-encrypt internally, or do model servers terminate TLS directly?

2) In-transit protection between services: do you use mTLS for internal RPCs between edge and model runtime? If so, what cert lifecycle/rotation process is in place?

3) Key management and rotation: high-level architecture for KMS/HSM usage (KEK wrapping, DEK lifecycle), rotation schedule (KEK/DEK frequency), emergency rotation process, and where rotation events are logged. Would you be able to provide a sample rotation audit log and a diagram? SIG references: v1.3 Section 3.2.1 - please indicate evidence locations.

If you can point me to a sample log and a brief narrative (or attestation) covering emergency rotation and BYOK customers, that will help our reviewers.

Appreciate fast turnaround — compliance needs this by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Rachel Adams
Senior InfoSec Analyst
SecureBank

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Adams <soc@securebank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: ephemeral session keys / TLS termination / rotation evidence

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear list. Summary below and attached artifacts: redwood_kms_rotation_diagram.pdf (architecture diagram) and a redacted sample rotation log (rotation_audit_log_sample.csv).

Short answers up front:
- TLS termination: TLS is terminated at our edge (regional LBs). We re-establish TLS to the model runtime using internal TLS; all internal connections are mutually authenticated (mTLS) for control planes and RPC traffic. We do not expose plaintext over any internal network.
- In-transit protection: mTLS (TLS 1.3) with server and client certs issued by our internal CA. Certificates are rotated via automated workflows; short-lived certs (14-day validity) for service-to-service tokens and 90-day rotation for longer-lived node certificates.
- KMS/HSM and rotation: Customer data encryption uses envelope encryption. Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) are generated per-customer and per-tenant resource and are wrapped by a Key Encryption Key (KEK) managed in an HSM-backed KMS. We use an external FIPS-validated HSM provider for root KEK custody (HSM model: vendor H3, FIPS 140-2/140-3 Level 3). KEKs rotate on a scheduled 90-day cadence. DEKs are rotated on major lifecycle events (rekey on key compromise, subscription change, or customer request) and during major model rollouts where re-encryption is required. Emergency rotation (compromise) triggers immediate KEK rotation and bulk DEK rewraps; this process is orchestrated by our crypto-ops runbook and requires approvals from two custodians.

Evidence provided: diagram (attached) shows TLS termination points, mTLS paths, and KMS/HSM placement; rotation_audit_log_sample.csv contains timestamped wrap/unwrap events and actor IDs (redacted). We also maintain SIG-specific evidence pages (link in metadata).

I'll leave Dev and Marcus to add low-level telemetry and cert-config details.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: ephemeral session keys / TLS termination / rotation evidence

Olga/Rachel — adding specifics from crypto-ops:

- TLS details: we enforce TLS 1.3 only inbound and outbound. Edge LB terminates client TLS and establishes mTLS to an internal ingress cluster. Cipher suite policy follows our hardened profile (AEAD suites only, e.g., TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384).
- mTLS: internal services present short-lived X.509 certs minted by our internal CA (automated via our cert-mgmt service). Rotation: certs are reissued automatically; we maintain certificate transparency-style records internally and publish a signed bundle for auditors on request.
- KMS/HSM: root KEKs are generated, stored, and used within the HSM. We perform periodic key ceremony activities (documented) for KEK generation/escrow. All KEK rotation events are recorded in our immutable audit ledger and mirrored to an external S3 bucket with object-lock for tamper-evidence. Retention: 2 years for rotation logs by default; longer by contract.
- Rotation frequency and policy: KEK scheduled rotation: 90 days; DEK rotation: event-driven (rotate-on-deploy option available per-customer). For BYOK customers we support wrapping customer KEKs in HSM; customer retains root key material when configured.
- Emergency rotation: documented in runbook RCN-401; process includes immediate revocation, forced cert reissue, KEK rewrap, and live migration of DEKs. Approval gates: primary custodian + security lead (Neha).

Attached: rotation_audit_log_sample.csv (redacted), which shows wrap/unwrap, actor, timestamps.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Crypto Ops Engineer
marcus_lin@redwood.com
